description.narrative:
The Love Alliance, a new five-year programme (2021-2025), is based on an unwavering commitment to protecting, promoting and fulfilling sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) globally, unifying people who use drugs, sex workers and LGBTIQ+ movements, and amplifying the diversity of voices in these communities.
Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Love Alliance brings together national thought leaders GALZ, SANPUD and Sisonke, regional grantmakers UHAI EASHRI, AFE and ISDAO, with the global network of people living with HIV (GNP+) and the Netherlands-based administrative lead Aidsfonds.
Together, we advocate for adequate levels of funding and for taking truly human rights-based programmes to scale. We take this opportunity to prioritise and invest in challenging the structural barriers of underfunding, criminalisation and exclusion of us in all our diversity.

comment.narrative: LA networks have become civil accountability spaces where communities share challenges and solutions. Young female sex workers have been supported in addressing the lack of health care facilities with national budget holders. partners engagement in Community- Led Monitoring under the aegis of PEPFAR and Global fund, made it possible to safeguard the interests of LA communities by maintaining the role of communities in the CLM processes.)

PWUD through ZCLDN continuously holds service providers accountable for delivering PWUD friendly services. Advocacy and leadership skills-building workshop for 10 PWUD representatives from 5 provinces resulted in a strengthened capacity of the community in conducting the community-led monitoring (CLM) process in that they used the leadership skills to monitor how PWUD are treated in the health setups, treatment services given for PWUD and any aftercare services provided to people who use drugs.

Through NAPs’ advocacy in the country and the region, key achievements were made to hold the government accountable to its commitment to protecting the independence of civil society. This was facilitated by engaging ally parliamentarians in using the law and constitution to challenge the passing of the PVO bill.
Reduction in the number of reported SGBV and stigma & discrimination against key populations at selected public sector health delivery sites and across 4 provinces (This is a 5-year target)
